problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ -8 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(1,-1)$, $(1,0)$ and $(-2,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$ 

- $(10,20)$
- $(4,-8)$
- $(-6,6)$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -8 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,1)$, $(2,1)$ and $(1,0).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(-2,1)$
- $(-8,4)$
- $(3,6)$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -8 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -12 & -2 \\ 4 & 6 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-8,4)$, $(-12,6)$ and $(-2,1).$ 

So, the correct answer is "I and II only."
